deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio is the draft of §1 (the historical survey) of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (written 1853/54, published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867). The text on this page agrees almost verbatim with the published version. The page is historical narrative. Its only mathematical content is the statement of the Fourier series and the Euler–Fourier coefficient formulas.

(1) Summary of the vibrating-string controversy.
- Euler introduced 'arbitrary' (graphically given) functions into analysis. On the basis of geometric intuition he applied the calculus to them (the general solution y = φ(x+αt) + ψ(x−αt) with arbitrary φ, ψ).
- Lagrange accepted Euler's results, including the geometric construction of the motion of the string. He wanted, however, a derivation founded on the method of limits ('Grenzenmethode').
- d'Alembert accepted Euler's way of treating the differential equation. He disputed Euler's results because, for arbitrary functions, one cannot know whether the derivatives are continuous.
- All three rejected the generality of Daniel Bernoulli's trigonometric solution. d'Alembert had to claim that even an analytically given periodic function need not be representable by a trigonometric series. Lagrange believed he could prove that such functions are representable.

(2) Fourier.
- About fifty years passed without essential progress. The margin replacement reads: 'in der Frage über die analytische Darstellbarkeit willkürlicher Functionen'.
- Then Fourier observed that in
  f(x) = Σ_{n≥1} a_n sin nx + ½ b_0 + Σ_{n≥1} b_n cos nx
  the coefficients are given by
  a_n = (1/π) ∫_{−π}^{π} f(x) sin nx dx,
  b_n = (1/π) ∫_{−π}^{π} f(x) cos nx dx.
- [My filling] These formulas follow by multiplying the series by sin mx or cos mx, integrating term by term over [−π, π], and using orthogonality:
  ∫ sin nx sin mx = π δ_{nm},
  ∫ cos nx cos mx = π δ_{nm} (m, n ≥ 1),
  ∫ sin nx cos mx = 0,
  ∫ cos² 0x = 2π, which explains the factor ½ on b_0.
- Fourier saw that these formulas still make sense for completely arbitrary f. He inserted discontinuous ('broken-line') functions and obtained series that in fact reproduced the function's values.

(3) Reception of Fourier's claim.
- Fourier stated the general theorem in his first heat memoir to the Académie (21 Dec 1807). The aged Lagrange opposed it decisively. Per Dirichlet's oral communication, a document about this is said to exist in the Academy archive.
- Poisson (author of the Bulletin philomathique report on Fourier's memoir, and in his Traité de mécanique No. 323, p. 638) nonetheless repeatedly attributed the representation to a passage in Lagrange's vibrating-string memoir. Riemann ascribes this to the Fourier–Poisson rivalry and announces a return to Lagrange's memoir.

(4) Next page.
- Riemann shows that Lagrange's formula y = Σ_{k=1}^{n} 2 ∫ Y sin kXπ dX · sin kxπ is really a finite trigonometric interpolation. In it the '∫ dX' denotes a sum Σ ΔX over the nodes X = j/(n+1).

(5) Margins.
- Bibliographic references: Misc. Taur. II p. 18; d'Alembert, Opuscules I (1761) p. 16 art. VII–XX and p. 42 art. XXIV; Misc. Taur. III p. 221 art. XXV; Bull. soc. philomath. I p. 112; Dirichlet's oral communication; Poisson, Traité de mécanique; the note that the Bulletin report is by Poisson.
errors: No mathematical errors. The coefficient formulas are correct and consistent with the ½ b_0 normalization.

Historical nuance, not a slip by the standards of 1854: the integral formulas for the coefficients were not first found by Fourier. Clairaut (1759) and especially Euler (1777, published 1798) had obtained them via orthogonality. Riemann's attribution of the 'Bemerkung' to Fourier follows the tradition of Dirichlet's circle. Fourier's real novelty was applying the formulas to arbitrary, including discontinuous, functions.
Riemann's explanation of Poisson's attribution to Lagrange as rivalry is an interpretive judgment, not a demonstrable fact.
The remark that Fourier's series 'in der That stets den Werth der Function gab' glosses over behaviour at jump points, where the series gives the mean value. This is harmless in a historical survey.

results.what: Fourier series of a function on [−π,π] with coefficients a_n=(1/π)∫f sin nx dx, b_n=(1/π)∫f cos nx dx (with ½b_0 term)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (1777) and Clairaut (1759) for the formulas; Fourier (1807/1822) for their application to arbitrary functions

results.what: Historical account of the vibrating-string controversy (Euler, d'Alembert, D. Bernoulli, Lagrange) and of the reception of Fourier's 1807 memoir (Lagrange's opposition, Poisson's attribution to Lagrange)
results.modern_name: History of the vibrating-string controversy / Fourier's 1807 memoir
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own published Habilitationsschrift §1 (1867) is a standard source for this account

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of the historical introduction of Riemann's well-known Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series, matching the published text nearly word for word. The only formulas are the standard Fourier coefficient formulas.

checkable.asserts: Normalization giving the 1/pi factor in a_n.
Explains the 1/2 in front of b_0 when b_0=(1/pi)∫f dx.
Fourier sine coefficients of the discontinuous function sign(x) on (-pi,pi): a_n = 2(1-(-1)^n)/(n*pi).
The Fourier series of sign(x) evaluated at x=1 is close to 1, illustrating Fourier's claim for a 'broken-line' function.
Discrete orthogonality underlying Lagrange's finite interpolation formula (next page): sum_{j=1}^{n} sin^2(k j pi/(n+1)) = (n+1)/2, here n=3, k=1.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Obgleich Euler zuerst…' should read 'so hatte Euler zuerst diese Functionen in die Analysis eingeführt, und, auf geometrische Anschauung gestützt, die Infinitesimalrechnung auf sie angewandt.' This continues the sentence from the previous page ('Um also schliesslich … zusammenzustellen,') and matches the published text.
'beschränkte sich, die Richtigkeit seiner Resultate anzufechten' – correct as written; the published version adds 'darauf'.

The marginal note 'Die Frage über die analytische Darstellbarkeit willkürlicher Functionen … ein wesentlicher Fortschritt gemacht wurde' replaces the main-text phrase 'in der Behandlung (ganz) willkürlicher Functionen'. The published text reads 'ohne dass in der Frage über die analytische Darstellbarkeit willkürlicher Functionen ein wesentlicher Fortschritt gemacht wurde.'
'bemerklich machte {+kundthat+}': the interlinear word is 'kundthat', written as a variant of 'bemerklich machte'.
'[-Nichts-] {+Dessenungeachtet+}': the struck word is uncertain; 'Dessenungeachtet verweist Poisson…' agrees with the published text.
The marginal reference 'p. d'Alembert' is an interlinear addition above 'Opuscules mathématiques'.
The struck marginal item after it is illegible; probably an aborted 'ibid.'-type reference.
